bib.title: Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection

question: Why do one-stage dense detectors trail two-stage detectors in accuracy, and can a change to the loss close the gap?
hypothesis: Extreme foreground-background class imbalance during training is the main obstacle; down-weighting well-classified examples in the cross entropy removes it.
contributions: Identify class imbalance as the central cause of the one-stage accuracy gap
Propose the Focal Loss, a cross entropy scaled by (1-pt)^gamma
Design RetinaNet, a simple FPN-based one-stage detector, that matches or beats two-stage detectors on COCO

method.summary: RetinaNet (ResNet-FPN backbone, class subnet and box subnet) is trained on all ~100k anchors per image with an alpha-balanced focal loss plus smooth L1 box loss, with the classifier bias initialised to a prior pi=.01. Ablations on COCO compare CE, alpha-CE, FL and OHEM, anchor density, and depth/scale.

datasets.name: COCO trainval35k
datasets.size: 80k train images plus a random 35k subset of the 40k val images
datasets.preprocessing: horizontal flip only; Table 2 model also uses scale jitter

models.name: RetinaNet (ResNet-50-FPN / ResNet-101-FPN / ResNeXt-32x8d-101-FPN)
models.architecture: one-stage FCN: ResNet+FPN (P3-P7, 256 channels), class subnet (4x 3x3 conv 256 + ReLU, then 3x3 conv KA, sigmoid), box subnet (same, 4A linear outputs, class-agnostic), separate parameters, subnets shared across levels
models.init_from: ImageNet1k pretrained ResNet-50/101 released by He et al.; new FPN layers as in FPN; new conv layers bias 0, Gaussian sigma=0.01; final class conv bias -log((1-pi)/pi)

other.anchors: A=9 per level (3 aspect ratios {1:2,1:1,2:1} x scales {2^0,2^(1/3),2^(2/3)}), areas 32^2 to 512^2 on P3-P7, covering 32-813 px
other.pyramid: P3-P5 from C3-C5, P6 3x3 stride-2 conv on C5, P7 ReLU + 3x3 stride-2 conv on P6; no P2

models.name: Faster R-CNN variants, YOLOv2, SSD, DSSD, R-FCN

training.objective: focal loss FL(pt) = -alpha_t (1-pt)^gamma log(pt) summed over ~100k anchors, normalised by number of anchors assigned to a ground-truth box, plus smooth L1 box regression
training.lr_schedule: divided by 10 at 60k and again at 80k iterations
training.hardware: 8 GPUs (type not stated for training; inference timed on Nvidia M40)
training.wall_clock: 10 to 35 hours for the models in Table 1e

inference.decoding: decode boxes from at most 1k top-scoring predictions per FPN level after thresholding confidence at 0.05; merge levels; NMS threshold 0.5
inference.samples: single model, single run per setting; no seeds or variance reported

metrics.name: COCO AP
metrics.definition: standard COCO bounding-box average precision (AP50, AP75, APS/M/L also reported)

eval.protocol: ablations on minival with ResNet-50/101, 600 px; main results on test-dev. No repeats, seeds or significance tests stated.

evidence.quote: synchronized SGD over 8 GPUs with a total of 16 images per minibatch (2 images per GPU)
at each level we add anchors of sizes {20, 21/3, 22/3}

limits: Single runs, no seeds or variance; gains of 0.2-0.4 AP (alpha .5 vs .25, FL vs FL*) are within unreported noise.
Binary focal loss only; multi-class extension asserted to work well but not shown.
Hinge loss attempt was unstable, no numbers.
Authors concede faster, more accurate results came after publication from a Faster R-CNN variant (Detectron); high frame-rate regime left to special network design.
Training GPU type and total compute not stated; test-dev result needs scale jitter and 1.5x longer schedule.

terms.definition: FL(pt) = -(1-pt)^gamma log(pt), a dynamically scaled cross entropy whose factor decays to zero as confidence in the correct class increases
a single unified network of a backbone and two task-specific subnetworks (classification, box regression)
